record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Algebraic form of known superintegrable examples
record.original_question: After transporting the superintegrable system to the Lie algebra e(n+1)=so(n+1)+R^(n+1), what do the symmetric operators C_i: so(n+1)→so(n+1) appearing in Hamiltonians of the form H=tr M^2+V(x) and F_i=tr C_i(M)M+V_i(x) look like in known examples?

evidence.quote: Q9 ... It would be interesting to see how the collection of operators Ci looks like in known examples.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Euclidean Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(n+1) = \mathfrak{so}(n+1) \oplus \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, with elements written as pairs $(M,x)$ where $M \in \mathfrak{so}(n+1)$ is a skew-symmetric $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ matrix and $x \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. Equip $\mathfrak{e}(n+1)^*$ with its standard linear (Lie–Poisson) bracket. Consider Hamiltonian systems of the form
$$H(M,x) \;=\; \operatorname{tr}(M^2) + V(x),$$
admitting a maximal collection of functionally independent first integrals (i.e. a superintegrable system) of the form
$$F_i(M,x) \;=\; \operatorname{tr}\bigl(C_i(M)\,M\bigr) + V_i(x), \qquad i = 1, 2, \ldots,$$
where each $C_i : \mathfrak{so}(n+1) \to \mathfrak{so}(n+1)$ is a symmetric linear operator (with respect to the trace form $\langle A,B\rangle = -\tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}(AB)$) and the $V_i : \mathbb{R}^{n+1} \to \mathbb{R}$ are smooth potentials.

Problem: For each known superintegrable system on a constant-curvature space (sphere or Euclidean space) of dimension $n$ that can be transported to $\mathfrak{e}(n+1)$ in this manner, explicitly describe the family of symmetric operators $\{C_i\}$ on $\mathfrak{so}(n+1)$ together with the corresponding potentials $V$, $V_i$. Identify the algebraic structure (e.g. commutation relations, joint diagonalizability, dependence on auxiliary parameters) of the collection $\{C_i\}$ in these examples, and characterize which collections of symmetric operators $C_i : \mathfrak{so}(n+1) \to \mathfrak{so}(n+1)$ can arise from a superintegrable system of the above form.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an exploratory research question asking for explicit descriptions of operator collections in known superintegrable examples. No published systematic classification or tabulation answering it appears in standard sources; it remains open.

status_evidence.title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems relating Nijenhuis geometry with integrable and superintegrable systems.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open research problem with no resolution provided.
